title: Pico Board Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Clocks and Watches with AI
description: Hover and click the main parts of a Raspberry Pi Pico W drawing to learn what each one does, then take a quiz that hides the labels and tracks the parts you missed.

educational.topic: Parts of the Raspberry Pi Pico W board
learningObjectives: Identify the RP2040 chip, USB connector, BOOTSEL button, on-board LED, wireless module, and pin rows on a Pico W.
Recall the purpose of each of those parts.
Recall which later projects in the book use each part.
prerequisites: Read the Raspberry Pi Pico section of Chapter 1.

accessibility.notes: Screen-reader description provided; all controls are standard HTML elements.

controls.label: Board hotspots
controls.description: Shows the name of the part under the pointer (Explore mode only).

controls.label: Board hotspots
controls.description: Explore mode: shows the part description. Quiz mode: answers the current question.

controls.label: Quiz me / Stop quiz / Explore
controls.description: Starts a six-question quiz with labels hidden, or returns to Explore mode.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Labeled exploration followed by self-quiz with retrieval practice
keyQuestions: Which button do you hold down while plugging in the Pico to install MicroPython?
Which part makes the Pico W different from a plain Pico?
Where do you connect a display to the Pico?
commonMisconceptions: Thinking the whole board is called the RP2040. The RP2040 is only the black chip; the board is the Pico.
Thinking the BOOTSEL button is a reset button. It selects USB-drive mode when pressed during power-up.
Thinking a plain Pico has WiFi. Only the Pico W has the wireless module.
assessmentOpportunities: Students score 6 out of 6 on the built-in quiz.
Students can name the part needed for each task: installing firmware (BOOTSEL), WiFi time sync (wireless module), and wiring a display (pins).
Students can explain the difference between the RP2040 chip and the Pico W board.
